# Yumma CSS Docs

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/README.md

# Yumma CSS Docs

[Yumma CSS](https://yummacss.com) is a utility framework whose class names are derived from CSS property names by one rule. `d-f` is `display: flex`, `jc-sb` is `justify-content: space-between`: initials of the property, initials of the value. If you know CSS, you already know Yumma CSS.

[Documentation](https://yummacss.com/docs) • [Playground](https://play.yummacss.com) • [GitHub](https://github.com/yummacss/yummacss) • [X](https://x.com/yummacss)

## Contributing

> [!NOTE]
> Please note that the following steps are only required in the event that you wish to contribute to the development of the software documentation or to address a software malfunction (bug).

To start the docs site in development mode, from the project root, run:

```bash
# install dependencies
pnpm i
# start development
pnpm d
```

This runs both the Next.js dev server and Yumma CSS in watch mode.

```bash
pnpm build
```

## Resources

Yumma CSS is part of a growing ecosystem of tools and complementary projects:

**[Yumma UI:](https://yummacss.com/ui)** A collection of ready-to-use UI components built with Base UI and styled with Yumma CSS.
<br/>
**[Yumma CSS Playground:](https://play.yummacss.com)** An interactive environment to experiment with Yumma CSS utilities right in your browser.
<br/>
**[Yumma CSS IntelliSense:](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=yumma-css.yummacss-intellisense)** VS Code extension that provides auto-completion, hover previews, and smart diagnostics.
<br/>
**[Eclipsa:](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=yumma-css.eclipsa)** A dark VS Code theme crafted for readability and style.

# colors.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/colors.mdx

order: 5
title: Colors
description: "Reference for all built-in color families & shades."

import { COLOR_FAMILIES, SHADE_LABELS } from "@/utils/colors";

## Default Palette

Yumma CSS provides {COLOR_FAMILIES.length} color families, each with {SHADE_LABELS.length} shades.

<Palette data={COLOR_FAMILIES} />

## Use Color Utilities

Apply color system utilities to style your elements.

```tsx
<div className="bg-red …"></div>
<div className="bg-green …"></div>
<div className="bg-blue …"></div>
```

## Use Color Shades

Each color family generates 13 values from a single base hex. The base color has no suffix. Shades `1–6` mix progressively more white, and shades `7–12` mix progressively more black.

| Suffix    | Direction |
|--------   |-----------|
| `1 to 6`  | Lightest  |
| (none)    | Base      |
| `7 to 12` | Darkest   |

The step size is controlled by `percentage.light` and `percentage.dark` in your config. Both default to `14`.

```tsx
<div className="bg-red-5 …"></div>
<div className="bg-green-5 …"></div>
<div className="bg-blue-5 …"></div>
```

## Use Opacity Modifiers

Target specific opacity values across color utilities. Opacity variants range from `0` to `95` in increments of `5`.

```tsx
<div className="bg-indigo-3/80 …"></div>
<div className="bg-indigo/60 …"></div>
<div className="bg-indigo-9/40 …"></div>
```

## Custom Colors

Extend or override the default palette using the `theme.colors` configuration option.

<Stepper>
  <Step title="Configure Custom Colors">
    ```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4-9}
    import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

    export default defineConfig({
      theme: {
        colors: {
          background: "#f5f6f7", // add new color family
          blue: "#1a73e8", // overrides the default blue.
        },
      },
    });
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Use Custom Colors">
    The bundler plugins pick up config changes automatically. If you use `yummacss watch`, restart it to see the changes.

    ```html "bg-background" "c-blue"
    <div className="bg-background …">
      <h1 className="c-blue …">Good evening</h1>
    </div>
    ```
  </Step>
</Stepper>

## Custom Color Shades

Override the default shade percentages using the `theme.colors.percentage` configuration option. The compiler automatically generates color shades (from 1 to 12) using the defined `percentage.light` and `percentage.dark` values.

<Stepper>
  <Step title="Configure Custom Colors">
    ```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={9-12}
    import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

    export default defineConfig({
      theme: {
        colors: {
          background: "#f5f6f7",
          blue: "#1a73e8",
        },
        percentage: {
          light: 16, // default is 14
          dark: 16, // default is 14
        },
      },
    });
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Use Custom Colors">
    The bundler plugins pick up config changes automatically. If you use `yummacss watch`, restart it to see the changes.

    ```html title="page.html"
    <div className="bg-background-6 …">
      <h1 className="c-blue-5 …">Good evening</h1>
    </div>
    ```
  </Step>
</Stepper>

---

# configuration.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/configuration.mdx

order: 3
title: Configuration
description: Configure Yumma CSS for your project.

## Install the CLI

Yumma CSS includes the Yumma CLI, a powerful tool for generating production-ready styles.

```bash
pnpm add yummacss -D
```

## Create Your Configuration File

Initialize a configuration file in your project.

```bash
pnpx yummacss init
```

This creates a `yumma.config.mjs` file at your project root. The same configuration file powers the CLI & the bundler plugins (`@yummacss/vite` & `@yummacss/postcss`).

```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4-5}
import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

export default defineConfig({
  source: [""],
  output: "",
});
```

### Source

A collection of paths for your template files (e.g., `.js`, `.tsx`, `.html`). The CLI scans these files for utilities to include in the final CSS file.

<Hint icon="info">
  Use glob patterns to include subfolders & specific file types.
</Hint>

```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4}
import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

export default defineConfig({
  source: ["./src/**/*.html"],
});
```

### Output

Specifies the output path for the compiled CSS file.

<Hint icon="info">
  Only the CLI uses `output`. The bundler plugins ignore it & inject the
  generated CSS through the `@yummacss;` marker instead.
</Hint>

```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4}
import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

export default defineConfig({
  output: "./src/styles.css",
});
```

### Normalize

Determines whether to include base styles normalization.

```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4}
import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

export default defineConfig({
  normalize: true, // default: true
});
```

### Prefix

Prepends a custom string to all generated Yumma CSS utility classes, effectively namespacing them to avoid collisions.

```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4}
import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

export default defineConfig({
  prefix: "ui",
});
```

<Hint icon="info">
  When a prefix is set, all utilities must include it-including entries in the
  `safelist`. For example, if your prefix is `ui`, use `ui-bg-red` instead of
  `bg-red`.
</Hint>

```html
<button class="ui-bg-indigo ui-c-white ui-p-4 ui-br-sm">Prefixed Button</button>
```

### Theme

Extends or overrides default design tokens.

#### Colors

Define custom color families. The compiler automatically generates shades (from 0 to 9) unless a full palette is explicitly provided.

<Hint icon="info">
  Use `percentage` to control how much the shade is lightened or darkened.
</Hint>

```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4-12}
import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

export default defineConfig({
  theme: {
    colors: {
      brand: "#9333EA",
      percentage: {
        light: 14,
        dark: 14,
      },
    },
  },
});
```

#### Screens

Define custom media query breakpoints or override existing ones.

```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4-13}
import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

export default defineConfig({
  theme: {
    screens: {
      sm: "40rem",
      md: "48rem",
      lg: "64rem",
      xl: "80rem",
      xxl: "96rem",
      "3xl": "112rem",
    },
  },
});
```

### Safelist

An array of utility classes that should always be generated in the final CSS output, regardless of whether they are present in your source files. Use this for classes that are added dynamically via JavaScript.

<Hint icon="info">
  Use `safelist` for classes generated dynamically at runtime. For example, in
  React, a template literal like `d-f` cannot be detected by
  the file scanner, making a safelist necessary.
</Hint>

```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4}
import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

export default defineConfig({
  safelist: ["bg-red", "c-white", "fw-700"],
});
```

## Generate Styles

The CLI scans files specified in `source` & generates a CSS file based on the utilities used.

### HTML Input

```jsx title="index.html"
<button class="bg-white c-black bw-1">Button</button>
```

### CSS Output

Running the `build` or `watch` command generates the following CSS:

```css title="styles.css"
.bg-white {
  background-color: #ffffff;
}

.bw-1 {
  border-width: 1px;
}

.c-black {
  color: #000000;
}
```

## CLI Commands

The Yumma CSS CLI provides commands to manage your project.

<Hint icon="info">
  Create a `yumma.config.mjs` file before running these commands. If you
  haven't, run `yummacss init`.
</Hint>

### Build

Compile your Yumma CSS files once.

```bash
npx yummacss build
```

### Watch

Watch for file changes & recompile automatically.

```bash
npx yummacss watch
```

---

# ide-support.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/ide-support.mdx

order: 4
title: IDE Support
description: "Get IDE support for Yumma CSS."

Speed up development with the official extensions. [Yumma CSS IntelliSense](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=yumma-css.yummacss-intellisense) provides auto-completion, hover previews & smart diagnostics directly in your editor.

## Visual Studio Code

Install the official [VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=yumma-css.yummacss-intellisense) to enable these features.

## Features

### IntelliSense

Get auto-completion suggestions for Yumma CSS utility classes as you type.

![IntelliSense auto-completion](/blog/yummacss-intellisense-completion.png)

### Hover Previews

View exact CSS declarations by hovering over any class in your code.

![Hover previews](/blog/yummacss-intellisense-hover.png)

### Smart Diagnostics

Identify overlapping styles & conflicting classes in real-time.

![Smart diagnostics](/blog/yummacss-intellisense-diagnostics.png)

### Conflict Detection

Yumma CSS IntelliSense detects when multiple classes set the same CSS property. For example, `bg-indigo bg-red` triggers a warning because both utilities set `background-color`. Conflicts are scoped per-variant, so `bg-red h:bg-indigo` does not conflict as they apply under different conditions.

### Class Sorting

Automatically organize your utility classes to maintain a consistent & readable codebase.

#### Sorting Order

Classes are organized by category in the following order: Layout → Positioning → FlexboxGrid → BoxModel → Background → Colors → BorderOutline → Typography → Effects → Transition → Interactivity → Table → SVG.

#### Variant Grouping

Variant classes like `h:bg-red` stay grouped with their base utility rather than being sorted independently. Orphan variants-those with no matching base class-are placed at the end of the class list.

#### How to Trigger

- **On Save**: Classes sort automatically when saving (`Ctrl+S`).
- **Command Palette**: Run `Yumma CSS: Sort Classes` from the Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P`).

### Quick Fixes

Resolve conflicts with 1-click quick fixes.

![Quick fixes](/blog/yummacss-intellisense-quick-fixes.png)

## Other Editors

The extension also supports other VS Code-based editors:

- [Cursor](https://www.cursor.com/)
- [VSCodium](https://vscodium.com/)
- [Trae](https://www.trae.sh/)
- [Windsurf](https://codeium.com/windsurf)
- [Antigravity](https://antigravity.dev/)

---

# installation.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/installation.mdx

order: 2
title: Installation
description: Install Yumma CSS using a bundler plugin, the CLI, or CDN.

## Set up Yumma CSS

Follow these steps to get started with Yumma CSS.

<Tabs defaultValue="vite">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTab value="vite">With Vite</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab value="nextjs">With Next.js</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab value="cli">With CLI</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab value="cdn">With CDN</TabsTab>
  </TabsList>

<TabsPanel value="vite">

Use the `@yummacss/vite` plugin with Vite & Vite-based frameworks like SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, & Solid. Generated CSS is rebuilt automatically as you work.

<Stepper>
  <Step title="Install Yumma CSS">
    ```bash
    pnpm add yummacss @yummacss/vite -D
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Add the Plugin">
    Register the plugin in your Vite configuration.

    ```ts title="vite.config.ts" mark={2,5}
    import { defineConfig } from "vite";
    import yummacss from "@yummacss/vite";

    export default defineConfig({
      plugins: [yummacss()],
    });
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Configure Sources">
    Specify the locations/paths of your project files in the config file.

    ```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4}
    import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

    export default defineConfig({
      source: ["./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"],
    });
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Add the Marker">
    Add the `@yummacss;` marker to your CSS entry file. The plugin replaces it with generated CSS.

    ```css title="src/styles.css"
    @yummacss;
    ```

  </Step>
</Stepper>

</TabsPanel>

<TabsPanel value="nextjs">

Use the `@yummacss/postcss` plugin with Next.js. It works with both Turbopack & Webpack through the built-in PostCSS support.

<Stepper>
  <Step title="Install Yumma CSS">
    ```bash
    pnpm add yummacss @yummacss/postcss -D
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Configure PostCSS">
    Register the plugin in your PostCSS configuration.

    ```mjs title="postcss.config.mjs" mark={3}
    export default {
      plugins: {
        "@yummacss/postcss": {},
      },
    };
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Configure Sources">
    Specify the locations/paths of your project files in the config file.

    ```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4}
    import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

    export default defineConfig({
      source: ["./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"],
    });
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Add the Marker">
    Add the `@yummacss;` marker to your global CSS file. The plugin replaces it with generated CSS.

    ```css title="globals.css"
    @yummacss;
    ```

  </Step>
</Stepper>

<Hint icon="info">
  The PostCSS plugin works anywhere PostCSS runs - not just Next.js.
</Hint>

</TabsPanel>

<TabsPanel value="cli">

Prefer generating a plain CSS file? Install Yumma CSS with your favorite package manager & use the CLI:

<Stepper>
  <Step title="Install Yumma CSS">
    ```bash
    pnpm add yummacss -D
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Initialize Configuration">
    Create a configuration file in your project.

    ```bash
    pnpx yummacss init
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Configure Sources">
    Specify the locations/paths of your project files in the config file.

    ```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4-5}
    import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

    export default defineConfig({
      source: ["./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"],
      output: "./src/styles.css",
    });
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Build styles">
    Start using Yumma CSS classes, then generate your styles.

    ```bash
    pnpx yummacss build
    ```

  </Step>
</Stepper>

</TabsPanel>

<TabsPanel value="cdn">

Import Yumma CSS directly into your HTML file via CDN for quick prototyping.

<Stepper>
  <Step title="Import Script">

    ```html
    <script src="https://unpkg.com/@yummacss/runtime"></script>
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Start Styling">

    ```html title="index.html"
    <body class="bg-black">
      <h1 class="c-white">Hello World</h1>
    </body>
    ```

  </Step>
</Stepper>

</TabsPanel>
</Tabs>

---

# media-queries.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/media-queries.mdx

order: 7
title: Media Queries
description: Use media queries to create responsive layouts.

## Mobile-First Approach

By default, all base utilities support responsive variants. Use breakpoints like `@sm:*`, `@md:*`, `@lg:*`, `@xl:*` & `@xxl:*` to apply specific rules to different screen sizes.

```html ins={2} del={1}
<h1 className="… @sm:ta-c">Good evening!</h1>
<h1 className="ta-c … @sm:ta-l">Good evening!</h1>
```

Yumma CSS breakpoints reference:

| Prefix | Min Width          | CSS Rule                       |
| ------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| `@sm`  | `40 rem` (640 px)  | `@media (min-width: 40 rem)`   |
| `@md`  | `48 rem` (768 px)  | `@media (min-width: 48 rem)`   |
| `@lg`  | `64 rem` (1024 px) | `@media (min-width: 64 rem)`   |
| `@xl`  | `80 rem` (1280 px) | `@media (min-width: 80 rem)`   |
| `@xxl` | `96 rem` (1536 px) | `@media (min-width: 96 rem)`   |

### Customize Breakpoints

You can extend or override the default media query breakpoints using the `theme.screens` configuration option in your `yumma.config.mjs` file.

<Stepper>
  <Step title="Create a config file">
    ```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4-8}
    import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

    export default defineConfig({
      theme: {
        screens: {
          "3xl": "112rem",
        },
      },
    });
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Use Custom Breakpoints">
    The bundler plugins pick up config changes automatically. If you use `yummacss watch`, restart it to see the changes.
    ```html "@3xl:d-b"
    <div className="d-none @3xl:d-b"></div>
    ```
  </Step>
</Stepper>

## Use Media Queries

Resize your browser window to see how these elements respond to viewport width.

```tsx "@sm:d-b" "@md:d-b" "@lg:d-b" "@xl:d-b" "@xxl:d-b"
<p className="d-b … @sm:d-none">Small screen</p>
<p className="d-none @md:d-none … @sm:d-b">Medium screen</p>
<p className="d-none @lg:d-none … @md:d-b">Large screen</p>
<p className="d-none @xl:d-none … @lg:d-b">Extra large screen</p>
<p className="d-none … @xxl:d-b">Double extra large screen</p>
```

## Touch Devices

The `pc:*` variant targets devices with a coarse pointer (typically touch screens). Use this to apply larger tap targets & touch-friendly spacing.

<Hint icon="hand_tap">
  Activates on touch-enabled devices with coarse pointer input.
</Hint>

```html "@pc:p-6"
<button type="button" class="p-4 bg-indigo c-white @pc:p-6">
  Larger padding on touch devices
</button>
```

Touch Device Reference:

| Prefix | Media Query                | Description   |
| ------ | -------------------------- | ------------- |
| `@pc:`  | `@media (pointer: coarse)` | Touch devices |

# negative-values.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/negative-values.mdx

order: 8
title: Negative Values
description: "Use negative values to create "

## Use Negative Values

Yumma CSS supports negative values for specific utilities like margins, positioning & letter spacing. Use the `(prefix)--(value)` syntax to apply a negative value.

## Margin

Use negative margins to overlap elements or create unique layouts. Negative margins are available for all margin utilities (`m-`, `mt-`, `mr-`, `mb-`, `ml-`, `mx-` & `my-`).

```tsx "ml--4"
<div className="z-1 …">A</div>
<div className="ml--4 z-2 …">B</div>
<div className="ml--4 z-3 …">C</div>
```

## Positioning

Apply negative offsets to position elements outside their parents or create overlapping effects. This works with `t-`, `r-`, `b-`, `l-` & `i-` utilities.

```tsx "t--4" "l--4"
<div className="p-r …">
  <div className="p-a t--4 l--4 …"></div>
</div>
```

## Z-Index

Negative z-index values allow you to place elements behind their siblings or parents. Use `zi--(value)` to target negative stack levels.

```tsx "zi--10"
<div className="p-r …">
  <div className="p-a zi--10 …"></div>
  <span>Background Layer</span>
</div>
```

## Sign Toggle

Specific utilities in Yumma CSS use a sign-toggle behavior. Instead of simply prepending a negative sign, the double-dash `--` syntax flips the current sign of the utility's value. This is particularly useful for utilities where the default value is already negative.

### Letter Spacing

Utilities like `ls-1` & `ls-2` are defined with negative CSS values. Using the sign-toggle syntax `ls--1` or `ls--2` flips these to positive values, resulting in wider spacing instead of tighter spacing.

| Class  | Standard Value | Negated Class | Negated Value |
| ------ | -------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| `ls-0` | `0`            | `ls--0`       | `0`           |
| `ls-1` | `-0.05 em`     | `ls--1`       | `0.05 em`     |
| `ls-2` | `-0.025 em`    | `ls--2`       | `0.025 em`    |
| `ls-3` | `0.025 em`     | `ls--3`       | `-0.025 em`   |
| `ls-4` | `0.05 em`      | `ls--4`       | `-0.05 em`    |
| `ls-5` | `0.1 em`       | `ls--5`       | `-0.1 em`     |

<Hint icon="info">
  Sign-toggle behavior applies to any utility where the defined CSS value
  already starts with a negative number.
</Hint>

```tsx "ls-1" "ls--1"
<p className="ls-1 …">Standard (Tight)</p>
<p className="ls--1 …">Negated (Wide)</p>
```

---

# normalize.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/normalize.mdx

order: 6
title: Normalization
description: Normalize CSS styles across browsers.

## Box Sizing

Apply a modern box model and remove browser defaults to simplify layout consistency.

```css
*,
:before,
:after {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  border: 0 solid;
}

* {
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
}
```

## Document

Set a default system font, improve rendering, & apply accessible line-height.

```css
html {
  font-family:
    system-ui,
    -apple-system,
    Segoe UI,
    Roboto,
    Helvetica Neue,
    Noto Sans,
    Liberation Sans,
    Arial,
    sans-serif,
    Apple Color Emoji,
    Segoe UI Emoji,
    Segoe UI Symbol,
    Noto Color Emoji;
}

body {
  -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
  font-family: inherit;
  line-height: 1.5; /* 4 */
}
```

## Media Elements

Ensure images & videos behave predictably in all layouts.

```css
canvas,
img,
picture,
svg,
video {
  max-width: 100%;
  display: block;
}
```

## Form Elements

Normalize form controls for visual consistency & accessibility.

```css
button,
input,
optgroup,
select,
textarea {
  background-color: transparent;
  padding: 0.5rem;
  font-family: inherit;
}
```

Add a default border to form elements that do not have a class attribute.

```css
button:not([class]),
input:not([class]),
optgroup:not([class]),
select:not([class]),
textarea:not([class]) {
  border: 1px solid #bfc2c7;
}
```

Apply consistent focus styles to interactive elements.

```css
:is(a, button, input, select, summary, textarea):focus {
  outline: 2px solid transparent;
}
```

Set a minimum height for textareas without a defined `rows` attribute.

```css
textarea:not([rows]) {
  min-height: 10em;
}
```

Ensure the buttons have a pointer cursor.

```css
button {
  cursor: pointer;
}
```

Disabled states

```css
button:disabled,
input:disabled,
select:disabled,
textarea:disabled {
  cursor: not-allowed;
  opacity: 0.5;
}
```

## Typography

Improve rendering, wrapping, & default font behavior.

```css
h1,
h2,
h3,
h4,
h5,
h6,
p {
  overflow-wrap: break-word;
}

h1,
h2,
h3,
h4,
h5,
h6 {
  text-wrap: balance;
  font-size: 1rem;
  font-weight: 600;
}

p {
  text-wrap: pretty;
}
```

Chrome, Edge, & Safari bold weight correction:

```css
b,
strong {
  font-weight: 700;
}
```

Default font size across browsers:

```css
small {
  font-size: 80%;
  line-height: 1.4;
}
```

<br />

```css
pre,
code,
kbd,
samp {
  font-family: monospace;
  font-size: 1em;
}
```

```css
a {
  color: inherit;
  text-decoration: none;
}
```

## Lists

Remove default list styles for clean, customizable lists.

```css
ol,
ul {
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}
```

## Tables

Standardize table header styling for better readability.

```css
th {
  font-size: 1rem;
  font-weight: 600;
}
```

## Miscellaneous

Fix minor browser quirks and improve default styles for common elements.

```css
hr {
  border-top: 1px solid #bfc2c7;
  height: 0;
  margin: 1em 0;
}
```

Ensure details and summary elements display correctly.

```css
details {
  display: block;
}

summary {
  display: list-item;
}
```

### Disable Base Styles

Base styles are enabled by default to disable it set `normalize` to `false` in `yumma.config.mjs`.

```mjs title="yumma.config.mjs" mark={4}
import { defineConfig } from "yummacss";

export default defineConfig({
  normalize: true,
});
```

---

# overflow-wrap.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/overflow-wrap.mdx

order: 197

# philosophy.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/philosophy.mdx

order: 1
title: Philosophy
description: Why Yumma CSS maps class names directly to CSS properties.

## Derivation, not aliasing

Most utility frameworks introduce a vocabulary layer. Class names *represent* CSS values through human-readable aliases.

```html "d-if ai-c mbs-6 ml-4 c-black fw-600" "display: inline-flex; align-items: center; margin-block-start: 1.5rem; margin-left: 1rem; color: #000000; font-weight: 600;"
<!-- 123 chars -->
<div style="display: inline-flex; align-items: center; margin-block-start: 1.5rem; margin-left: 1rem; color: #000000; font-weight: 600;">Blog</div>

<!-- 35 chars -->
<h1 class="d-if ai-c mbs-6 ml-4 c-black fw-600">Blog<h1>
```

With Yumma CSS, if you know CSS, you already know the class name. Each class is derived from the CSS property and value you would have written anyway.

## About semantics

Semantic frameworks optimize for readability, `font-semibold` reads very naturally. But readability comes at a cost: you need to memorize a separate vocabulary on top of CSS. `font-semibold` doesn't tell you it's `font-weight: 600`. `items-center` doesn't tell you it's `align-items`, and so on and so forth.

The derivation rule is consistent and predictable. Once you know that `jc` is the initials of `justify-content` and `c` is the initial of `center`, you can derive `jc-c` without looking anything up. The same rule gives you `jc-fe` (flex-end), `jc-sb` (space-between), and every other value.

There is no vocabulary to memorize on top of CSS. There is only CSS, compressed.

## How does it works?

Every class in Yumma CSS maps to exactly one CSS property.

```css
.ai-c {
  align-items: center;
}

.c-white {
  color: #ffffff;
}

.d-f {
  display: flex;
}

.fw-600 {
  font-weight: 600;
}
```

## One class, one property

Every class maps to exactly one CSS property. The generated CSS is transparent and predictable by inspection.

```html
// 1.1kB
<button class="px-3 py-2 bg-indigo h:bg-indigo-8 bc-indigo-7 c-white br-md bw-1 fw-600 c-p">
  Add to Cart
</button>
```

## When Yumma CSS fits

- You know CSS well and want class names that reflect it directly.
- You prefer explicit values (`fw-600`) over semantic aliases (`font-semibold`).
- You want predictable output without indirections.
- You're building a design system where consistency and transparency matter.
- You want no new vocabulary to memorize.

## When it may not fit

- You rely heavily on a large pre-built component ecosystem.
- Your team is deeply familiar with another framework's vocabulary and the switching cost outweighs the benefit.
- You need official multi-framework UI kits out of the box.

---

# pseudo-classes.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/pseudo-classes.mdx

order: 9
title: Pseudo Classes
description: "Use pseudo classes to style elements."

## Active

Represents an element activated by the user (e.g., clicking a button).

<Hint icon="cursor_click">
  Try clicking and holding the button to see the active state.
</Hint>

```tsx "a:bg-indigo-7"
<button className="… a:bg-indigo-7">
  Press me
</button>
```

## Focus

Represents an element that received focus via click, tap, or the **Tab** key.

<Hint icon="cursor_click">
  Try clicking on the input field to see how the border color and outline
  change.
</Hint>

```tsx "f:oc-indigo-4" "f:oo-2" "f:os-s" "f:ow-2"
<button className="… f:oc-indigo-4 f:oo-2 f:os-s f:ow-2">
  Click me
</button>
```

## Hover

Matches an element when the user interacts with it using a pointing device.

<Hint icon="hand_pointing">
  Try hovering over the button to see how the background color changes.
</Hint>

```tsx "h:bg-indigo-7"
<button className="… h:bg-indigo-7">
  Hover me
</button>
```

## Focus Visible

Triggers when an element matches `:focus` & the browser determines focus should be evident.

<Hint icon="keyboard">
  Try using Tab to focus the button with your keyboard.
</Hint>

```tsx "fv:ow-2" "fv:oc-indigo-2"
<button className="… fv:ow-2 fv:oc-indigo-2">
  Focus me
</button>
```

## Focus Within

Matches an element if the element or any of its descendants are focused.

<Hint icon="cursor_click">
  Try clicking on the input field to see the container's border change.
</Hint>

```tsx "fw:oc-indigo-6"
<div className="… fw:oc-indigo-6">
  <input placeholder="Focus me" />
</div>
```

## Checked

Represents radio, checkbox, or option elements toggled to an "on" state.

```tsx "c:bg-indigo-4"
<input type="checkbox" checked />
<label className="… c:bg-indigo-4">
  Checked checkbox
</label>
```

## Disabled

Represents disabled elements that cannot be activated or receive focus.

<Hint icon="cursor">
  Elements with the `disabled` attribute use `cursor: not-allowed` by default in
  [Normalize](/docs/normalize).
</Hint>

```tsx "d:bg-silver-4" "d:c-silver-9"
<button className="… d:bg-silver-4 d:c-silver-9" disabled>
  Disabled
</button>
```

Here's a reference for all the pseudo-variants available in Yumma CSS.

| Pseudo-class     | Prefix | Description                                 |
| ---------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `:active`        | `a:*`  | Applied when the element is being pressed   |
| `:checked`       | `c:*`  | Applied when a radio or checkbox is checked |
| `:disabled`      | `d:*`  | Applied when the element is disabled        |
| `:empty`         | `e:*`  | Applied when the element has no children    |
| `:focus`         | `f:*`  | Applied when the element receives focus     |
| `:focus-visible` | `fv:*` | Applied when focused via keyboard           |
| `:focus-within`  | `fw:*` | Applied when element or child has focus     |
| `:hover`         | `h:*`  | Applied when the element is hovered         |
| `:first-child`   | `fc:*` | Applied when it's the first child           |
| `:invalid`       | `i:*`  | Applied when the element value is invalid   |
| `:indeterminate` | `in:*` | Applied when state is indeterminate         |
| `:last-child`    | `lc:*` | Applied when it's the last child            |
| `:nth-child`     | `nc:*` | Applied when matches nth-child(n)           |
| `:required`      | `r:*`  | Applied when the element is required        |
| `:read-only`     | `ro:*` | Applied when the element is read-only       |
| `:valid`         | `v:*`  | Applied when the element value is valid     |

---

# pseudo-elements.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/pseudo-elements.mdx

order: 10
title: Pseudo Elements
description: "Use pseudo elements to style elements."

Pseudo-element variants allow you to style `::before`, `::after`, `::selection`, and `::placeholder` elements using simple prefixes.

## Before

Creates a pseudo-element that is the first child of the selected element.

<Hint icon="info">
  Pseudo Elements require content to be visible. Make sure to set content via
  CSS or inline styles when using `::before`.
</Hint>

```html "b::p-a" "b::bg-indigo/10"
<div class="p-r p-8 b::p-a b::i-0 b::bg-indigo/10">Styled content</div>
```

## After

Creates a pseudo-element that is the last child of the selected element.

<Hint icon="info">
  Like `::before`, the `::after` pseudo-element requires content to be visible.
</Hint>

```html "a::p-a" "a::c-indigo"
<div class="p-r a::p-a a::c-indigo">Styled content</div>
```

## Selection

Applies styles to highlighted/selected text.

<Hint icon="cursor_text">
  Try selecting the text below to see the custom selection styling.
</Hint>

```tsx "s::bg-indigo"
<p className="… s::bg-indigo">
  Select this text to see custom selection colors!
</p>
```

## Placeholder

Styles the placeholder text for `input` or `textarea` elements.

<Hint icon="cursor_click">
  Try focusing on the input to see the placeholder styling.
</Hint>

```tsx "p::c-silver"
<input className="… p::c-silver" placeholder="Enter your email…" />
```

Here's a reference for all the pseudo-element variants available in Yumma CSS:

| Pseudo-element  | Prefix | Description                                     |
| --------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `::after`       | `a::*` | Styles the last child pseudo-element            |
| `::before`      | `b::*` | Styles the first child pseudo-element           |
| `::selection`   | `s::*` | Styles the portion of text that is selected     |
| `::placeholder` | `p::*` | Styles placeholder text in inputs and textareas |

---

# scroll-padding.mdx

Source: https://github.com/yumma-lib/yumma-css-docs/blob/release/src/content/docs/scroll-padding.mdx

order: 152
title: Scroll Padding
description: "Set the scroll padding for snapping & alignment."

<Baseline path="css.properties.scroll-padding" />

<Reference category="interactivity" name="scroll-padding" />

### Responsiveness
